metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.method: Manual inspection of programs/swift/micro (mb00-mb11) and programs/swift/adversarial samples. Score reflects intrinsic language conciseness relative to idiomatic Swift style, independent of tooling maturity.
observations: Type inference and trailing-closure syntax reduce boilerplate versus C++/Java for equivalent numeric workloads (e.g. mb04.swift LCG struct + workload function is compact).
Struct value semantics avoid explicit copy-constructor boilerplate seen in more verbose OOP languages.

Swift stdlib lacks a native printf-style float formatter, forcing Foundation import and String(format:) for %.16e output; this is a language-level expressiveness gap counted against conciseness since other languages handle this natively.
No unnecessary copies observed; arrays use copy-on-write value semantics, loops use direct indexing consistent with idiomatic performant Swift.

Adversarial samples (ADV-01..26) are short edge-case snippets; explicit optional-unwrapping (guard let, as?, do/catch) adds modest syntactic ceremony versus implicit-null languages, but this is an intentional safety trade-off rather than pure verbosity.

metric.readability.method: Qualitative review of naming, structural clarity, comment density, and control-flow directness in the same Swift micro/adversarial corpus.
observations: Consistent descriptive naming (Lcg, workload, nextUnit) and doc-comment convention aid readability.
Structured timing API (ContinuousClock().measure) reads as a clear closure rather than manual timer start/stop pairs.
guard/if-let/optional chaining in adversarial samples produce very readable control flow for null/error handling versus manual null checks in C-like languages.
Foundation import required purely for numeric formatting is a minor readability blemish, borrowing C-style format-string semantics inconsistent with Swift's native string interpolation.
Struct/method organization (private state, mutating func) makes value semantics and mutation intent explicit, aiding reasoning about program behavior.
Overall idiomatic modern Swift reads clearly; denser than Python but clearer than typical template-heavy C++.
